question: What is the shortcut key to open 'Paste Special' dialogue box in Microsoft Word?
solution:
The Correct Answer is ​__Ctrl + Alt + V__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Microsoft applications, you can invoke the "Paste Special" dialog box by using the combination of Ctrl + Alt + V keys.__
 
• __Paste Special: __The Paste Special command is used when you want to specify how the data you paste into a cell or range is formatted, or if you want to paste only specific aspects of the data you are copying. For example, you might only want to paste the formatting from a copied cell, or perhaps only the formula.
 
• __Key combination:__ You can access this feature by pressing Ctrl + Alt + V after copying or cutting the data you want to paste. This opens the "Paste Special" dialog box which gives you a variety of options for how you wish to paste your data.
 
• __Diverse Options__: The options available in the Paste Special dialog box vary depending on the application you are using. Typically, these options include choices like paste values only, paste formatting only, transpose (which switches rows to columns and vice versa), multiply (which multiplies copied data by data in the pasted location), and more.
 
• __Common across MS Applications:__ The Paste Special feature, including its keyboard shortcut, is common across multiple Microsoft Office Applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.
 
• __Difference between Paste and Paste Special__: The difference between the regular paste function and the Paste Special function is in the customization. While a regular paste (Ctrl + V) will simply duplicate all of the data as it is, Paste Special allows you to control what aspects of the data you want to duplicate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Alt + P closes all open documents in Adobe Photoshop, except for the current document
 
• Ctrl+V is a keyboard shortcut that pastes the contents of the clipboard into a computer document
 
• Ctrl+Alt+C is a keyboard shortcut that inserts the copyright symbol
